title: Prefix hit-curve modeling and staged TTL optimizer for KV caching
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Prefix/KV caching is a major driver of token-level cost variance. Existing rules are either static TTLs per model or coarse heuristics that underutilize cache for long-tail prefixes and over-cache ephemeral prefixes. Goal: Ship an automated recommendation and safe-apply flow that (1) computes a per-prefix hit-curve (hit-rate vs TTL) from historical traces, (2) generates an economical TTL gradient with explicit marginal-cost savings per ms of latency impact, and (3) applies changes with staged safety (shadow evaluation, canary, fast rollback). Scope: telemetry-based modeling, canonicalization rules for cache keys, simulation harness, a recommender that outputs a ranked list of prefix -> TTL suggestions, and a config apply orchestration with dry-run and safety gates.
acceptance_criteria: Hit-curve generator produces stable curves for >85% of prefix groups (by QPS) over a 7-day window
Recommender outputs TTL suggestions with estimated cost delta and expected median latency delta
Dry-run simulator (replays sampled traffic) predicts cost reduction within +/-10% of live results
Safe-apply flow includes shadow mode, 5% canary, automated rollback triggers, and idempotent apply semantics
Documentation and runbook published in Confluence with example PRs and dashboard links
simulation_summary: We ran the hit-curve estimator on a 10M request sample from 2026-02-01..2026-02-07. Results: long-tail prefixes (60% of unique prefixes, 15% of QPS) have sub-5% baseline hit rates until TTL > 12s; mid-tail prefixes show a steep plateau at 4s-8s. A candidate TTL gradient (per-prefix recommendation) simulated on replay traffic indicates a projected 11.6% token-cost savings with median latency +6ms and p95 +22ms. Sensitivity: if traffic shifts (hot prefix spike), cost savings drop to 4% and tail latency may increase beyond SLO; hence safety budget set to 1.5% error margin and conservative TTL floor policy.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Internal dry-run — run KV-Scout recommender against last 7 days, generate CSV and reviewer dashboard
Step 1: Shadow apply — deploy TTL changes in shadow for 48h (no evictions), collect hit-rate and cost proxies
Step 2: Canary 1 — 1% traffic with 12h monitoring window and automated rollback triggers
Step 3: Canary 2 — 5% traffic for 24h if Canary 1 passes; continue to 25% then 100% in stepped increments
Step 4: Post-apply verification — compare projected vs actual cost and tail latency; run automatic backfill if regressions found
Step 5: Retrospective and tuning — weekly eval for 4 weeks to refine estimator hyperparameters
rollback_triggers: Absolute p95 latency increase > 35ms for the canary cohort vs baseline
Token-cost per minute worse than projected by >2x the expected error margin
Error-rate spike for requests that hit the cache key canonicalizer > 0.5% absolute
Recommender produced TTLs that increase evictions on top-k hot prefixes by >15% leading to tail thrash

notes: Novel parts: hit-curve (marginal hit-rate vs TTL) provides per-prefix marginal utility; TTL gradient minimizes cost under latency SLO. Avoids one-size-fits-all TTLs. Next: bake into Optimize recommendations UI and surface expected cost/latency tradeoffs in Console.
